# Results

## Summary Stats

- Find rating distributions in pg: 5--7.
- Find list of highest to lowest rated questions in pg: 7--8.

## Inter-Rater Reliability

Inter-rater reliability was assessed using Krippendorff's $\alpha$ (ordinal) across 
five raters and eight evaluation criteria. Overall agreement was low for both 
models (GPT-4 $\alpha$ = 0.173, GPT-5 $\alpha$ = 0.0462; pg: 11), falling well below the commonlly accepted threshold of 0.667 [cite @krippendorff]. Agreement varied considerably across criteria: Ambiguity, Factuality, and Narrativity showed near-zero or negative $\alpha$ values, indicating systematic disagreement, while Repetition, Generalization, and Recall showed relatively higher though still insufficient 
agreement (pg: 11--12). A sensitivity analysis excluding each rater individually showed that no single rater was responsible for the low agreement — the most impactful 
exclusion (R3) improved GPT-4 $\alpha$ from 0.173 to 0.323, but left GPT-5 largely unchanged (pg: 12--15). This suggests the disagreement is structural, likely reflecting the inherent 
subjectivity of certain criteria rather than individual rater error. Given this, 
all five raters were retained for subsequent analyses.

## Paired samples t-test

The Irrelevance criterion was excluded from inferential analyses due to a skewed distribution (ceiling effect), as inspection of its histogram revealed ratings concentrated at the higher end of the scale, violating the normality assumption.

A paired samples t-test was conducted to compare ratings between GPT-4 (*M* = 3.31, *SD* = 0.949) and GPT-5 (*M* = 3.35, *SD* = 0.955) across seven criteria. No significant overall difference was found (*t*(565) = -1.04,*p* = .299, mean diff = -0.049, 95% CI [-0.143, 0.044]).

Per-criterion analyses were conducted with Bonferroni correction applied(*$\alpha$* = .05/7 = .007). Two criteria showed significant differences after correction: GPT-4 was rated significantly higher on Narrativity (*t*(74) = 5.22, *p* < .001, *d* = 0.603), while GPT-5 was rated significantly higher on Factuality (*t*(74) = -3.20, *p* = .014, *d* = -0.370). Both represent medium effect sizes. Recall and Reduction showed uncorrected significant differences that did not survive Bonferroni correction (both *p* > .30 after correction).

A limitation of this study is the small number of raters (*n* = 5). However, given the Central Limit Theorem, the aggregated ratings are expected to approximate a normal distribution, supporting the validity of parametric testing.


# Data analysis R code

## Preprocessing

### Libraries
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggpubr)
library(irr)
library(effectsize)
```

### Get individual CSVs
```{r}
files <- list.files(pattern = "\\.csv$")
```

### Append into one CSV and convert to long format
```{r}
complete <- lapply(files, function(f) {
  read.csv(f) %>%
    mutate(Rater = tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f)))
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  relocate(Rater) %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(Rater, Question, Model),
    names_to = "Criteria",
    values_to = "Rating"
    )
# make sure ratings are numeric values
complete$Rating <- as.numeric(complete$Rating)
```

### View complete data
```{r}
view(complete)
head(complete)
```

## Summary

```{r}
summary(complete)

# grouped by model and criteria
complete %>% group_by(Model, Criteria) %>% 
  summarise(across(Rating, list(mean=mean, sd=sd, min=min, max=max),
                   na.rm = TRUE))
```


### Rating distribution per criteria
* check if data is normally distributed
```{r}
complete.filtered <- complete %>%
  filter(Model %in% c("GPT4", "GPT5")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Rating))

# Overall overlay histogram (all criteria combined)

ggplot(complete.filtered, aes(x = Rating, fill = Model)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 1,
    boundary = -0.5,
    color = "white",
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Model) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("GPT4" = "steelblue", "GPT5" = "tomato")) +
  geom_vline(
    data = complete.filtered %>%
      group_by(Model) %>%
      summarise(mean = mean(Rating, na.rm = TRUE)),
    aes(xintercept = mean, color = Model),
    linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("GPT4" = "steelblue", "GPT5" = "tomato")) +
  theme_pubr() +
  ggtitle("Overall Rating Distribution: GPT-4 vs GPT-5")

plot <- function(data, title) {
    ggplot(data, aes(x = Rating)) +
      
    geom_histogram(
      binwidth = 1,
      boundary = -0.5,
      fill = "steelblue",
      color = "white"
    ) +
      
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
      ) +
      
    geom_vline(
      data = data %>%
        group_by(Criteria) %>%
        summarise(mean = mean(Rating, na.rm = TRUE)),
      aes(xintercept = mean),
      colour = "deeppink",
      linewidth = 0.7
    ) +
      
    facet_wrap(~Criteria, ncol=4) +
    theme_pubr() +
    ggtitle(title)
}
  
plot(filter(complete, Model=="GPT4"), "GPT-4")
plot(filter(complete, Model=="GPT5"), "GPT-5")
```

## Inference

### Krippendorf's Alpha
* test for inter-rater agreement
```{r}
check_without_rater <- function(rater) {
  filtered <- complete.filtered %>% filter(Rater != rater)
  
  cat("Original rows:", nrow(complete.filtered), "\n")
  cat("Filtered rows:", nrow(filtered), "\n")
  cat("Remaining raters:", paste(unique(filtered$Rater), collapse = ", "), "\n\n")
  
  kripp.results <- filtered %>%
  group_by(Model, Criteria) %>% 
  group_modify(~{
    mat <- .x %>% 
      pivot_wider(names_from = Rater, values_from = Rating) %>% 
      select(-Question) %>% 
      as.matrix()
    
    result <- kripp.alpha(t(mat), method = "ordinal")
    tibble(alpha = result$value)
  }) %>% 
    mutate(excluded = rater)
  
  kripp.results.excl.overall <- filtered %>%
  group_by(Model) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    mat <- .x %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = c(Rater), values_from = Rating,
                  id_cols = c(Question, Criteria)) %>%
      select(-c(Question, Criteria)) %>%
      as.matrix()
    result <- kripp.alpha(t(mat), method = "ordinal")
    tibble(alpha = result$value)
  })
  
  cat("=== Excluding", rater, "===\n\n")
  cat("--- Per Model and Criteria ---\n")
  print(kripp.results)
  cat("\n--- Overall per Model ---\n")
  print(kripp.results.excl.overall)
  
  return(kripp.results)
}

kripp.results.overall <- complete.filtered %>%

  group_modify(~ {
    mat <- .x %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = c(Rater), values_from = Rating,
                  id_cols = c(Question, Criteria)) %>%
      select(-c(Question, Criteria)) %>%
      as.matrix()
    
    result <- kripp.alpha(t(mat), method = "ordinal")
    tibble(alpha = result$value)
  })

cat("=== Baseline Overall Alpha ===\n")
print(kripp.results.overall)

# 2. Per criteria alpha
kripp.results <- complete.filtered %>%
  group_by(Model, Criteria) %>% 
  group_modify(~{
    mat <- .x %>% 
      pivot_wider(names_from = Rater, values_from = Rating) %>% 
      select(-Question) %>% 
      as.matrix()
    
    result <- kripp.alpha(t(mat), method = "ordinal")
    tibble(alpha = result$value)
  })

cat("=== Per Model and Criteria ===\n")
print(kripp.results)

# 2. Sensitivity analysis
exclusion_resutls <- map_dfr(c("A", "K", "L", "S", "Y"), check_without_rater)

exclusion_resutls %>% 
  group_by(Model, Criteria) %>% 
  slice_max(alpha, n = 1) %>% 
  select(Model, Criteria, best_exclusion = excluded, alpha)

```

### Paired t-test
* test for model differences
```{r}
# make model ratings into wide format (for t-test)
complete_wide <- complete %>% 
  group_by(Rater, Question, Criteria, Model) %>% 
  summarise(Rating = mean(Rating, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Model,
    values_from = Rating
  )

head(complete_wide)

# Summarise by model
complete_wide %>%
  summarise(
    M_GPT4 = mean(GPT4, na.rm=TRUE), SD_GPT4 = sd(GPT4, na.rm=TRUE),
    M_GPT5 = mean(GPT5, na.rm=TRUE), SD_GPT5 = sd(GPT5, na.rm=TRUE)
  )

# overall
t.test(complete_wide$GPT4, complete_wide$GPT5, paired = TRUE)

# group differences across raters
t <- complete_wide %>%
  group_by(Rater) %>%
  summarise(
    t_test = list(t.test(GPT4, GPT5, paired = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# cohen's d
d_values <- complete_wide %>%
  group_by(Criteria) %>%
  summarise(
    cohens_d = mean(GPT4 - GPT5, na.rm = TRUE) / sd(GPT4 - GPT5, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# per criterion
t_criteria <- complete_wide %>%
  filter(Criteria != "Irrelevance") %>% # correction will apply for 7 tests
  group_by(Criteria) %>%
  summarise(
    M_GPT4    = mean(GPT4, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_GPT4   = sd(GPT4, na.rm = TRUE),
    M_GPT5    = mean(GPT5, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_GPT5   = sd(GPT5, na.rm = TRUE),
    test      = list(t.test(GPT4, GPT5, paired = TRUE)),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    t_stat    = map_dbl(test, ~ .x$statistic),
    df        = map_dbl(test, ~ .x$parameter),
    p_value   = map_dbl(test, ~ .x$p.value),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p_value, method = "bonferroni"),
    mean_diff = map_dbl(test, ~ .x$estimate),
    ci_low    = map_dbl(test, ~ .x$conf.int[1]),
    ci_high   = map_dbl(test, ~ .x$conf.int[2])
  ) %>%
  left_join(d_values, by = "Criteria") %>%
  select(-test)


print(t_criteria)
print(d_values)

```
